brief_problem: The kiosk class that does everything

runs.text: Each job belongs to the class that has the information to do it.
A single piece of the kiosk,
, reads the sales, computes the amounts, takes off the stock, applies the discount and writes the receipt. Every change, however small, touches that piece, and it already has
How is the work shared out?
Make a list of the jobs of
and write next to each one which data it needs to be done.

Computing an amount needs the price of the product. Taking off the stock needs how much is left. Gathering the total and applying the discount need what was sold. Writing the receipt needs the lines of each sale. Each job needs different data: that is the clue that there are different pieces.

entries.text: What goes in and what comes out?
The same as before: what changes is who does each part.
: bringing together what changes for the same reason.
Who has the information to do this?
That question, asked for each job, shares out the work.

blocks.description: Four cards. Product knows its price and computes the amount. Stock knows how much is left and takes away if there is enough. Receipt notes and prints the lines. Till registers the sale and gathers the total, and asks the other three for help.

caption.text: Each card says what a class knows or does and whom it asks for help.

runs.text: The outputs are the same that the single class gave for the same sales: the behaviour did not change, the sharing out did. And now each piece can be tested on its own:
with an exact stock and one that is not enough.
Each kiosk class does what its information allows, and the till coordinates the sale by asking them for help
Changing the format of the receipt touches only
. Adding a tax to the amount touches only
. With a single class, each of those changes touched the same file of 600 lines.

points.text: A responsibility is something a class knows or does; its collaborators are the classes it asks for help.
A responsibility card writes down a class, its job and whom it works with.

entries.text: is usually a job that belongs to another class.

A card that does not fit on the paper is a class that does too much.
